Hi Aisha,

- Typical cost per 1M tokens under different quantization profiles (fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit)
- How KV cache hit-rate assumptions change unit cost (e.g., 0%, 20%, 50%)

- Pilot credit structure / discounts for early-stage pilots and what counts toward commit

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pricing & architecture for inference-efficiency pilot

Hi Sophie — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. Quick answers up front, followed by a short worked example and a proposed pilot commercial path.

Recommendation summary:
- Quantization: 4-bit for non-sensitive model weights where possible (Q4_0/Q4_K_M), 8-bit as a conservative fallback. Expect ~1.6–2.1x reduction in per-token GPU cost vs fp16 depending on kernel set.
- KV cache: assume a realistic pilot hit rate of 20–30% for conversational flows; each 10% of hit-rate reduces per-token compute by roughly 6–8% in our benchmarks for your payload sizes.
- Batching: use adaptive batching with max batch size tuned to p95; for 150ms p95 we typically set max_batch_tokens ~2048 and a latency-aware timeout of 8–10ms for spikes.
- Pilot credits: propose a two-part structure (intro credit + commit band): 30% intro credit up to $12k, then tiered commit bands with stepped discounts for 3- and 6-month pilots.

Worked example (approximate):
Assumptions: 2M tokens/day, 30-day pilot -> 60M tokens. Model baseline fp16 unit = $X per 1k tokens (we’ll give exact in sheet). Using Q4 -> ~1.9x compute reduction -> cost ~0.53x fp16. With 25% KV cache hit -> further ~15% reduction on compute portion. Net: ~0.45x fp16. After intro credit (30% up to $12k) and a 10% pilot discount for a 3-month small commit, net pilot cost ~0.3–0.35x baseline — detailed numbers in pilot-pricing-sheet.xlsx.

Next steps:
1) I’ll loop in Connor for a quick procurement note on concession bands and approvals.
2) If that looks good, we can schedule a 45-minute commercial + ops walkthrough next week to lock down SLA/ops guardrails.

Attaching the pricing sketch for clarity (pilot-pricing-sheet.xlsx). Happy to convert this to a one-pager for procurement.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Sales Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

- If they commit to explicit quantization guidance (Q4-only for 50% of production traffic) and a KV cache target (>=25% hit-rate) we can treat that as a delivery milestone to qualify for an additional 5% rebate at renewal.
- Approvals: I have authority up to 12% discount; need product/finance sign-off for 15%+. Suggest Connor own finance calc and Neha sign off on the SLA/ops guardrail text.

Customer signals: mid-market buyer, cares a lot about predictable unit economics and compliance (SOC2). If they ask for more than 15% or non-standard term (data residency), we escalate.

Connor — please pull a quick expected margin delta for these concession tiers and confirm whether we can sleeve the intro credit out of our new pilot pool.

Sophie / procurement team — attaching the requested table inline below and the updated pricing sheet. Short notes at the top, then the table.

Notes:
- Numbers are approximations based on our standard model profile for summarization and your usage snapshot. We’re happy to run an exact ledger with a short proof pass but this should be procurement-ready.
- All unit compute costs exclude storage and networking; KV cache savings quoted are compute-only.

Concrete table (cost per 1M tokens) — compute-only, illustrative:
- fp16, KV 0%: $1,200 per 1M tokens
- 8-bit, KV 0%: $720 per 1M tokens
- 4-bit, KV 0%: $420 per 1M tokens

With KV caching applied (approximate multiplier):
- fp16, KV 20%: $1,080 per 1M tokens (10% reduction)
- 8-bit, KV 20%: $648 per 1M tokens
- 4-bit, KV 20%: $378 per 1M tokens

- fp16, KV 50%: $780 per 1M tokens (~35% reduction)
- 8-bit, KV 50%: $468 per 1M tokens
- 4-bit, KV 50%: $273 per 1M tokens

Batching sensitivity (p95 latency / cost impact):
- Avg batch size 8: baseline p95 ~140–160ms; cost multiplier ~1.0x
- Avg batch size 16: p95 ~160–200ms; cost multiplier ~0.92x
- Avg batch size 32: p95 ~220–350ms (not acceptable for 150ms p95); cost multiplier ~0.78x

Pilot commercial suggestion (final):
- Intro credit: 30% up to $12k applied on first invoice.
- Pilot discount: 12% for a 3-month pilot commit (no finance escalation needed).
- If Ledgerly commits to Q4 quantization for >=50% of pilot traffic and a KV hit-rate target >=25%, we’ll increase pilot discount to 15% and extend a one-time $8k renewal credit.

If that works I’ll send a short term sheet and DocuSign link (linked). Proposed next step: 45-minute call Wednesday 11/12 to lock the SOW and ops checklist.

Thanks — I’ll also pull procurement-friendly one-pager for your team.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Sales Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
